title: review: E6: Jev relevance ranking for memory recall and the handover snapshot — prune what the Planner reads, keep the rest verbatim
spec:
Compaction the jev-compactor way: score each candidate item for relevance to the current goal, drop the low ones, never summarize. Two Planner inputs qualify. Build on E2 (T-0214) and P3 (T-0204).
1. orchestrator/jev_rank.py rank(items: list[dict], goal_text: str, *, threshold=0.35, batch=40) -> list[dict]: each item {id, text}; asks Jev one noul question per item ('Is this entry relevant to the goal below?' with the goal as part of the state; batch up to 40 questions per request within the 64k limit), attaches p_relevant, returns items with p >= threshold sorted by p desc. jev.ask() None -> return items unchanged (fail-open) with p_relevant = None.
2. skills/planner/memory/scripts/recall.py index: new flag --goal "<text>" (or env ORCH_GOAL_TEXT): rank the hits with jev_rank before printing, print p as a fourth column, and print 'jev: off' when the client is disabled. Default output without --goal unchanged.
3. orchestrator/handover.py: the 'done (not merged)', 'failed' and 'Last events' groups pass through jev_rank against the open goal's title+spec with threshold 0.5 before rendering; merged and held groups are never pruned; the section header notes 'pruned N by jev' when N is greater than 0. Without Jev the output is byte-identical to today.
Tests: tests/test_jev_rank.py (batching, threshold, fail-open) and tests/test_handover.py::test_handover_prunes_with_jev and ::test_handover_unchanged_without_jev with jev.ask monkeypatched; tests/test_memory_skill.py::test_recall_goal_flag_ranks.

comments.issue: An HTTP-200 response whose `answers` map is missing an id (or has `noul: null`) yields `p_relevant=None`, and the `kept` filter on line 36 drops those items as if they scored 0. The callers' fail-open guard only fires when `len(ranked) == len(items)` and *all* are None, so a partial answer set is silently treated as 'these entries are irrelevant'. Concretely: Jev returns 200 with `{"answers": {}}` (or a body shape without `answers`, e.g. `{"result": ...}` after an API change) -> rank() returns [] -> handover._prune returns ([], N) -> the whole 'done (not merged)' and 'failed' lists vanish from plan.md and the header claims 'pruned N by jev'; recall.py prints '# 0 hits (showing 0)'. A 200 with an unexpected body is strictly worse than a network error, which is backwards for a module whose docstring is 'fail-open'. Unscored items should be kept (p_relevant=None -> keep), not dropped. No test covers a 200 with partial/absent answers — only all-or-nothing.

`_render_section` now performs blocking network I/O while the global bus flock is held (`write()` line 243 `with bus.locked():` -> line 249 `_render_section`), and `maybe_write` wraps that in a second acquisition on the daemon tick path. Per handover it issues up to 2 `jev.ask` calls per goal (failed + done groups) x MAX_GOALS=12, plus 1 for events = up to 25 sequential HTTPS round trips. At the default `timeout_s` of 5s with the 429/529 retry (+0.5s backoff) that is a worst case of roughly 2 minutes holding the flock; even a healthy Jev adds seconds. Every other orchestrator process — daemon dispatch, worker `bus.update`, task creation — blocks on that flock for the duration. Before this change `_render_section` was pure local sqlite reads. Render (and score) outside the lock, or cap/parallelize the calls.

`rank` promises 'never raises', but `answer.get("noul")` is unvalidated external API data. A non-numeric value (string "0.9", a dict, a bool-in-a-list) makes the `item["p_relevant"] >= threshold` comparison on line 36 or the `sort` on line 37 raise TypeError. That escapes rank() -> handover._prune -> `handover.write()` -> the daemon tick, aborting the handover write with the bus flock semantics of a raised exception, rather than degrading to the unranked list. Coerce with a float()/isinstance check and treat anything non-numeric as unscored.
